clauses.normalized_text: Streams in QUIC provide a lightweight, ordered byte-stream abstraction.
clauses.raw_text: Streams in QUIC provide a lightweight, ordered byte-stream abstraction.

clauses.normalized_text: There are two basic types of stream in QUIC.
clauses.raw_text: There are two basic types of stream in QUIC.

clauses.normalized_text: Unidirectional streams carry data in one direction: from the initiator of the stream to its peer; bidirectional streams allow for data to be sent in both directions.
clauses.raw_text: Unidirectional streams carry data in one direction: from the initiator of the stream to its peer; bidirectional streams allow for data to be sent in both directions.

clauses.normalized_text: Different stream identifiers are used to distinguish between unidirectional and bidirectional streams, as well as to create a separation between streams that are initiated by the client and server (see [stream-id]).
clauses.raw_text: Different stream identifiers are used to distinguish between unidirectional and bidirectional streams, as well as to create a separation between streams that are initiated by the client and server (see [stream-id]).

clauses.normalized_text: Either type of stream can be created by either endpoint, can concurrently send data interleaved with other streams, and can be cancelled.
clauses.raw_text: Either type of stream can be created by either endpoint, can concurrently send data interleaved with other streams, and can be cancelled.

clauses.normalized_text: Streams can be created by sending data.
clauses.raw_text: Streams can be created by sending data.

clauses.normalized_text: Other processes associated with stream management - ending, cancelling, and managing flow control - are all designed to impose minimal overheads.
clauses.raw_text: Other processes associated with stream management - ending, cancelling, and managing flow control - are all designed to impose minimal overheads.

clauses.normalized_text: For instance, a single STREAM frame ([frame-stream]) can open, carry data for, and close a stream.
clauses.raw_text: For instance, a single STREAM frame ([frame-stream]) can open, carry data for, and close a stream.

clauses.normalized_text: Streams can also be long-lived and can last the entire duration of a connection.
clauses.raw_text: Streams can also be long-lived and can last the entire duration of a connection.

clauses.normalized_text: Stream offsets allow for the octets on a stream to be placed in order.
clauses.raw_text: Stream offsets allow for the octets on a stream to be placed in order.

clauses.normalized_text: An endpoint MUST be capable of delivering data received on a stream in order.
clauses.raw_text: An endpoint MUST be capable of delivering data received on a stream in order.

clauses.normalized_text: Implementations MAY choose to offer the ability to deliver data out of order.
clauses.raw_text: Implementations MAY choose to offer the ability to deliver data out of order.

clauses.normalized_text: There is no means of ensuring ordering between octets on different streams.
clauses.raw_text: There is no means of ensuring ordering between octets on different streams.

clauses.normalized_text: Streams are individually flow controlled, allowing an endpoint to limit memory commitment and to apply back pressure.
clauses.raw_text: Streams are individually flow controlled, allowing an endpoint to limit memory commitment and to apply back pressure.

clauses.normalized_text: The creation of streams is also flow controlled, with each peer declaring the maximum stream ID it is willing to accept at a given time.
clauses.raw_text: The creation of streams is also flow controlled, with each peer declaring the maximum stream ID it is willing to accept at a given time.

clauses.normalized_text: An alternative view of QUIC streams is as an elastic “message” abstraction, similar to the way ephemeral streams are used in SST [SST], which may be a more appealing description for some applications.
clauses.raw_text: An alternative view of QUIC streams is as an elastic “message” abstraction, similar to the way ephemeral streams are used in SST [SST], which may be a more appealing description for some applications.

clauses.normalized_text: Streams are identified by an unsigned 62-bit integer, referred to as the Stream ID.
clauses.raw_text: Streams are identified by an unsigned 62-bit integer, referred to as the Stream ID.

clauses.normalized_text: Stream IDs are encoded as a variable-length integer (see [integer-encoding]).
clauses.raw_text: Stream IDs are encoded as a variable-length integer (see [integer-encoding]).

clauses.normalized_text: The least significant two bits of the Stream ID are used to identify the type of stream (unidirectional or bidirectional) and the initiator of the stream.
clauses.raw_text: The least significant two bits of the Stream ID are used to identify the type of stream (unidirectional or bidirectional) and the initiator of the stream.

clauses.normalized_text: The least significant bit (0x1) of the Stream ID identifies the initiator of the stream.
clauses.raw_text: The least significant bit (0x1) of the Stream ID identifies the initiator of the stream.

clauses.normalized_text: Clients initiate even-numbered streams (those with the least significant bit set to 0); servers initiate odd-numbered streams (with the bit set to 1).
clauses.raw_text: Clients initiate even-numbered streams (those with the least significant bit set to 0); servers initiate odd-numbered streams (with the bit set to 1).

clauses.normalized_text: Separation of the stream identifiers ensures that client and server are able to open streams without the latency imposed by negotiating for an identifier.
clauses.raw_text: Separation of the stream identifiers ensures that client and server are able to open streams without the latency imposed by negotiating for an identifier.

clauses.normalized_text: If an endpoint receives a frame for a stream that it expects to initiate (i.e., odd-numbered for the client or even-numbered for the server), but which it has not yet opened, it MUST close the connection with error code STREAM_STATE_ERROR.

clauses.raw_text: The second least significant bit (0x2) of the Stream ID differentiates between unidirectional streams and bidirectional streams.

clauses.normalized_text: Unidirectional streams always have this bit set to 1 and bidirectional streams have this bit set to 0.

clauses.raw_text: A receiver cannot renege on an advertisement; that is, once a receiver advertises a stream ID via a MAX_STREAM_ID frame, advertising a smaller maximum ID has no effect.

clauses.raw_text: Endpoints uses streams to send and receive data.

clauses.raw_text: Endpoints send STREAM frames, which encapsulate data for a stream.

clauses.raw_text: STREAM frames carry a flag that can be used to signal the end of a stream.

clauses.normalized_text: Streams are an ordered byte-stream abstraction with no other structure that is visible to QUIC.
clauses.raw_text: Streams are an ordered byte-stream abstraction with no other structure that is visible to QUIC.

clauses.normalized_text: The sending part of stream that the endpoint initiates (types 0 and 2 for clients, 1 and 3 for servers) is opened by the application or application protocol.
clauses.raw_text: The sending part of stream that the endpoint initiates (types 0 and 2 for clients, 1 and 3 for servers) is opened by the application or application protocol.

clauses.normalized_text: The “Ready” state represents a newly created stream that is able to accept data from the application.
clauses.raw_text: The “Ready” state represents a newly created stream that is able to accept data from the application.

clauses.normalized_text: Stream data might be buffered in this state in preparation for sending.
clauses.raw_text: Stream data might be buffered in this state in preparation for sending.

clauses.normalized_text: Sending the first STREAM or STREAM_BLOCKED frame causes a send stream to enter the “Send” state.
clauses.raw_text: Sending the first STREAM or STREAM_BLOCKED frame causes a send stream to enter the “Send” state.

clauses.normalized_text: An implementation might choose to defer allocating a Stream ID to a send stream until it sends the first frame and enters this state, which can allow for better stream prioritization.
clauses.raw_text: An implementation might choose to defer allocating a Stream ID to a send stream until it sends the first frame and enters this state, which can allow for better stream prioritization.

clauses.normalized_text: The sending part of a bidirectional stream initiated by a peer (type 0 for a server, type 1 for a client) enters the “Ready” state then immediately transitions to the “Send” state if the receiving part enters the “Recv” state.
clauses.raw_text: The sending part of a bidirectional stream initiated by a peer (type 0 for a server, type 1 for a client) enters the “Ready” state then immediately transitions to the “Send” state if the receiving part enters the “Recv” state.

clauses.normalized_text: In the “Send” state, an endpoint transmits - and retransmits as necessary - data in STREAM frames.
clauses.raw_text: In the “Send” state, an endpoint transmits - and retransmits as necessary - data in STREAM frames.

clauses.normalized_text: The endpoint respects the flow control limits of its peer, accepting MAX_STREAM_DATA frames.
clauses.raw_text: The endpoint respects the flow control limits of its peer, accepting MAX_STREAM_DATA frames.

clauses.normalized_text: An endpoint in the “Send” state generates STREAM_BLOCKED frames if it encounters flow control limits.
clauses.raw_text: An endpoint in the “Send” state generates STREAM_BLOCKED frames if it encounters flow control limits.

clauses.normalized_text: After the application indicates that stream data is complete and a STREAM frame containing the FIN bit is sent, the send stream enters the “Data Sent” state.
clauses.raw_text: After the application indicates that stream data is complete and a STREAM frame containing the FIN bit is sent, the send stream enters the “Data Sent” state.

clauses.normalized_text: From this state, the endpoint only retransmits stream data as necessary.
clauses.raw_text: From this state, the endpoint only retransmits stream data as necessary.

clauses.normalized_text: The endpoint no longer needs to track flow control limits or send STREAM_BLOCKED frames for a send stream in this state.
clauses.raw_text: The endpoint no longer needs to track flow control limits or send STREAM_BLOCKED frames for a send stream in this state.

clauses.normalized_text: The endpoint can ignore any MAX_STREAM_DATA frames it receives from its peer in this state; MAX_STREAM_DATA frames might be received until the peer receives the final stream offset.
clauses.raw_text: The endpoint can ignore any MAX_STREAM_DATA frames it receives from its peer in this state; MAX_STREAM_DATA frames might be received until the peer receives the final stream offset.

clauses.normalized_text: Once all stream data has been successfully acknowledged, the send stream enters the “Data Recvd” state, which is a terminal state.
clauses.raw_text: Once all stream data has been successfully acknowledged, the send stream enters the “Data Recvd” state, which is a terminal state.

clauses.normalized_text: From any of the “Ready”, “Send”, or “Data Sent” states, an application can signal that it wishes to abandon transmission of stream data.
clauses.raw_text: From any of the “Ready”, “Send”, or “Data Sent” states, an application can signal that it wishes to abandon transmission of stream data.

clauses.normalized_text: Similarly, the endpoint might receive a STOP_SENDING frame from its peer.
clauses.raw_text: Similarly, the endpoint might receive a STOP_SENDING frame from its peer.

clauses.normalized_text: In either case, the endpoint sends a RST_STREAM frame, which causes the stream to enter the “Reset Sent” state.
clauses.raw_text: In either case, the endpoint sends a RST_STREAM frame, which causes the stream to enter the “Reset Sent” state.

clauses.normalized_text: An endpoint MAY send a RST_STREAM as the first frame on a send stream; this causes the send stream to open and then immediately transition to the “Reset Sent” state.
clauses.raw_text: An endpoint MAY send a RST_STREAM as the first frame on a send stream; this causes the send stream to open and then immediately transition to the “Reset Sent” state.

clauses.normalized_text: Once a packet containing a RST_STREAM has been acknowledged, the send stream enters the “Reset Recvd” state, which is a terminal state.
clauses.raw_text: Once a packet containing a RST_STREAM has been acknowledged, the send stream enters the “Reset Recvd” state, which is a terminal state.

clauses.raw_text: [fig-stream-recv-states] shows the states for the part of a stream that receives data from a peer.

clauses.normalized_text: The states for a receive stream mirror only some of the states of the send stream at the peer.
clauses.raw_text: The states for a receive stream mirror only some of the states of the send stream at the peer.

clauses.normalized_text: A receive stream doesn’t track states on the send stream that cannot be observed, such as the “Ready” state; instead, receive streams track the delivery of data to the application or application protocol some of which cannot be observed by the sender.
clauses.raw_text: A receive stream doesn’t track states on the send stream that cannot be observed, such as the “Ready” state; instead, receive streams track the delivery of data to the application or application protocol some of which cannot be observed by the sender.

clauses.normalized_text: The receiving part of a stream initiated by a peer (types 1 and 3 for a client, or 0 and 2 for a server) are created when the first STREAM, STREAM_BLOCKED, RST_STREAM, or MAX_STREAM_DATA (bidirectional only, see below) is received for that stream.
clauses.raw_text: The receiving part of a stream initiated by a peer (types 1 and 3 for a client, or 0 and 2 for a server) are created when the first STREAM, STREAM_BLOCKED, RST_STREAM, or MAX_STREAM_DATA (bidirectional only, see below) is received for that stream.

clauses.normalized_text: The initial state for a receive stream is “Recv”.
clauses.raw_text: The initial state for a receive stream is “Recv”.

clauses.normalized_text: Receiving a RST_STREAM frame causes the receive stream to immediately transition to the “Reset Recvd”.
clauses.raw_text: Receiving a RST_STREAM frame causes the receive stream to immediately transition to the “Reset Recvd”.

clauses.normalized_text: The receive stream enters the “Recv” state when the sending part of a bidirectional stream initiated by the endpoint (type 0 for a client, type 1 for a server) enters the “Ready” state.
clauses.raw_text: The receive stream enters the “Recv” state when the sending part of a bidirectional stream initiated by the endpoint (type 0 for a client, type 1 for a server) enters the “Ready” state.

clauses.normalized_text: A bidirectional stream also opens when a MAX_STREAM_DATA frame is received.
clauses.raw_text: A bidirectional stream also opens when a MAX_STREAM_DATA frame is received.

clauses.normalized_text: Receiving a MAX_STREAM_DATA frame implies that the remote peer has opened the stream and is providing flow control credit.
clauses.raw_text: Receiving a MAX_STREAM_DATA frame implies that the remote peer has opened the stream and is providing flow control credit.

clauses.normalized_text: A MAX_STREAM_DATA frame might arrive before a STREAM or STREAM_BLOCKED frame if packets are lost or reordered.
clauses.raw_text: A MAX_STREAM_DATA frame might arrive before a STREAM or STREAM_BLOCKED frame if packets are lost or reordered.

clauses.normalized_text: Before creating a stream, all lower-numbered streams of the same type MUST be created.
clauses.raw_text: Before creating a stream, all lower-numbered streams of the same type MUST be created.

clauses.normalized_text: That means that receipt of a frame that would open a stream causes all lower-numbered streams of the same type to be opened in numeric order.
clauses.raw_text: That means that receipt of a frame that would open a stream causes all lower-numbered streams of the same type to be opened in numeric order.

clauses.normalized_text: This ensures that the creation order for streams is consistent on both endpoints.
clauses.raw_text: This ensures that the creation order for streams is consistent on both endpoints.

clauses.normalized_text: In the “Recv” state, the endpoint receives STREAM and STREAM_BLOCKED frames.
clauses.raw_text: In the “Recv” state, the endpoint receives STREAM and STREAM_BLOCKED frames.

clauses.normalized_text: Incoming data is buffered and can be reassembled into the correct order for delivery to the application.
clauses.raw_text: Incoming data is buffered and can be reassembled into the correct order for delivery to the application.

clauses.normalized_text: As data is consumed by the application and buffer space becomes available, the endpoint sends MAX_STREAM_DATA frames to allow the peer to send more data.
clauses.raw_text: As data is consumed by the application and buffer space becomes available, the endpoint sends MAX_STREAM_DATA frames to allow the peer to send more data.

clauses.normalized_text: When a STREAM frame with a FIN bit is received, the final offset (see [final-offset]) is known.
clauses.raw_text: When a STREAM frame with a FIN bit is received, the final offset (see [final-offset]) is known.

clauses.normalized_text: The receive stream enters the “Size Known” state.
clauses.raw_text: The receive stream enters the “Size Known” state.

clauses.normalized_text: In this state, the endpoint no longer needs to send MAX_STREAM_DATA frames, it only receives any retransmissions of stream data.
clauses.raw_text: In this state, the endpoint no longer needs to send MAX_STREAM_DATA frames, it only receives any retransmissions of stream data.

clauses.normalized_text: Once all data for the stream has been received, the receive stream enters the “Data Recvd” state.
clauses.raw_text: Once all data for the stream has been received, the receive stream enters the “Data Recvd” state.

clauses.normalized_text: This might happen as a result of receiving the same STREAM frame that causes the transition to “Size Known”.
clauses.raw_text: This might happen as a result of receiving the same STREAM frame that causes the transition to “Size Known”.

clauses.normalized_text: In this state, the endpoint has all stream data.
clauses.raw_text: In this state, the endpoint has all stream data.

clauses.normalized_text: Any STREAM or STREAM_BLOCKED frames it receives for the stream can be discarded.
clauses.raw_text: Any STREAM or STREAM_BLOCKED frames it receives for the stream can be discarded.

clauses.normalized_text: The “Data Recvd” state persists until stream data has been delivered to the application or application protocol.
clauses.raw_text: The “Data Recvd” state persists until stream data has been delivered to the application or application protocol.

clauses.normalized_text: Once stream data has been delivered, the stream enters the “Data Read” state, which is a terminal state.
clauses.raw_text: Once stream data has been delivered, the stream enters the “Data Read” state, which is a terminal state.

clauses.normalized_text: Receiving a RST_STREAM frame in the “Recv” or “Size Known” states causes the stream to enter the “Reset Recvd” state.
clauses.raw_text: Receiving a RST_STREAM frame in the “Recv” or “Size Known” states causes the stream to enter the “Reset Recvd” state.

clauses.normalized_text: This might cause the delivery of stream data to the application to be interrupted.
clauses.raw_text: This might cause the delivery of stream data to the application to be interrupted.

clauses.normalized_text: It is possible that all stream data is received when a RST_STREAM is received (that is, from the “Data Recvd” state).
clauses.raw_text: It is possible that all stream data is received when a RST_STREAM is received (that is, from the “Data Recvd” state).

clauses.normalized_text: Similarly, it is possible for remaining stream data to arrive after receiving a RST_STREAM frame (the “Reset Recvd” state).
clauses.raw_text: Similarly, it is possible for remaining stream data to arrive after receiving a RST_STREAM frame (the “Reset Recvd” state).

clauses.normalized_text: An implementation is able to manage this situation as they choose.
clauses.raw_text: An implementation is able to manage this situation as they choose.

clauses.normalized_text: Sending RST_STREAM means that an endpoint cannot guarantee delivery of stream data; however there is no requirement that stream data not be delivered if a RST_STREAM is received.
clauses.raw_text: Sending RST_STREAM means that an endpoint cannot guarantee delivery of stream data; however there is no requirement that stream data not be delivered if a RST_STREAM is received.

clauses.normalized_text: An implementation MAY interrupt delivery of stream data, discard any data that was not consumed, and signal the existence of the RST_STREAM immediately.
clauses.raw_text: An implementation MAY interrupt delivery of stream data, discard any data that was not consumed, and signal the existence of the RST_STREAM immediately.

clauses.normalized_text: Alternatively, the RST_STREAM signal might be suppressed or withheld if stream data is completely received.
clauses.raw_text: Alternatively, the RST_STREAM signal might be suppressed or withheld if stream data is completely received.

clauses.normalized_text: In the latter case, the receive stream effectively transitions to “Data Recvd” from “Reset Recvd”.
clauses.raw_text: In the latter case, the receive stream effectively transitions to “Data Recvd” from “Reset Recvd”.

clauses.normalized_text: Once the application has been delivered the signal indicating that the receive stream was reset, the receive stream transitions to the “Reset Read” state, which is a terminal state.
clauses.raw_text: Once the application has been delivered the signal indicating that the receive stream was reset, the receive stream transitions to the “Reset Read” state, which is a terminal state.

clauses.normalized_text: The sender of a stream sends just three frame types that affect the state of a stream at either sender or receiver: STREAM ([frame-stream]), STREAM_BLOCKED ([frame-stream-blocked]), and RST_STREAM ([frame-rst-stream]).
clauses.raw_text: The sender of a stream sends just three frame types that affect the state of a stream at either sender or receiver: STREAM ([frame-stream]), STREAM_BLOCKED ([frame-stream-blocked]), and RST_STREAM ([frame-rst-stream]).

clauses.normalized_text: A sender MUST NOT send any of these frames from a terminal state (“Data Recvd” or “Reset Recvd”).
clauses.raw_text: A sender MUST NOT send any of these frames from a terminal state (“Data Recvd” or “Reset Recvd”).

clauses.normalized_text: A sender MUST NOT send STREAM or STREAM_BLOCKED after sending a RST_STREAM; that is, in the “Reset Sent” state in addition to the terminal states.
clauses.raw_text: A sender MUST NOT send STREAM or STREAM_BLOCKED after sending a RST_STREAM; that is, in the “Reset Sent” state in addition to the terminal states.

clauses.normalized_text: A receiver could receive any of these frames in any state, but only due to the possibility of delayed delivery of packets carrying them.
clauses.raw_text: A receiver could receive any of these frames in any state, but only due to the possibility of delayed delivery of packets carrying them.

clauses.normalized_text: The receiver of a stream sends MAX_STREAM_DATA ([frame-max-stream-data]) and STOP_SENDING frames ([frame-stop-sending]).
clauses.raw_text: The receiver of a stream sends MAX_STREAM_DATA ([frame-max-stream-data]) and STOP_SENDING frames ([frame-stop-sending]).

clauses.normalized_text: The receiver only sends MAX_STREAM_DATA in the “Recv” state.
clauses.raw_text: The receiver only sends MAX_STREAM_DATA in the “Recv” state.

clauses.normalized_text: A receiver can send STOP_SENDING in any state where it has not received a RST_STREAM frame; that is states other than “Reset Recvd” or “Reset Read”.
clauses.raw_text: A receiver can send STOP_SENDING in any state where it has not received a RST_STREAM frame; that is states other than “Reset Recvd” or “Reset Read”.

clauses.normalized_text: However there is little value in sending a STOP_SENDING frame after all stream data has been received in the “Data Recvd” state.
clauses.raw_text: However there is little value in sending a STOP_SENDING frame after all stream data has been received in the “Data Recvd” state.

clauses.normalized_text: A sender could receive these frames in any state as a result of delayed delivery of packets.
clauses.raw_text: A sender could receive these frames in any state as a result of delayed delivery of packets.

clauses.normalized_text: A bidirectional stream is composed of a send stream and a receive stream.
clauses.raw_text: A bidirectional stream is composed of a send stream and a receive stream.

clauses.normalized_text: Implementations may represent states of the bidirectional stream as composites of send and receive stream states.
clauses.raw_text: Implementations may represent states of the bidirectional stream as composites of send and receive stream states.

clauses.normalized_text: The simplest model presents the stream as “open” when either send or receive stream is in a non-terminal state and “closed” when both send and receive streams are in a terminal state.
clauses.raw_text: The simplest model presents the stream as “open” when either send or receive stream is in a non-terminal state and “closed” when both send and receive streams are in a terminal state.

clauses.normalized_text: [stream-bidi-mapping] shows a more complex mapping of bidirectional stream states that loosely correspond to the stream states in HTTP/2 [HTTP2].
clauses.raw_text: [stream-bidi-mapping] shows a more complex mapping of bidirectional stream states that loosely correspond to the stream states in HTTP/2 [HTTP2].

clauses.normalized_text: This shows that multiple states on send or receive streams are mapped to the same composite state.
clauses.raw_text: This shows that multiple states on send or receive streams are mapped to the same composite state.

clauses.normalized_text: Note that this is just one possibility for such a mapping; this mapping requires that data is acknowledged before the transition to a “closed” or “half-closed” state.
clauses.raw_text: Note that this is just one possibility for such a mapping; this mapping requires that data is acknowledged before the transition to a “closed” or “half-closed” state.

clauses.normalized_text: If an endpoint is no longer interested in the data it is receiving on a stream, it MAY send a STOP_SENDING frame identifying that stream to prompt closure of the stream in the opposite direction.
clauses.raw_text: If an endpoint is no longer interested in the data it is receiving on a stream, it MAY send a STOP_SENDING frame identifying that stream to prompt closure of the stream in the opposite direction.

clauses.normalized_text: This typically indicates that the receiving application is no longer reading data it receives from the stream, but is not a guarantee that incoming data will be ignored.
clauses.raw_text: This typically indicates that the receiving application is no longer reading data it receives from the stream, but is not a guarantee that incoming data will be ignored.

clauses.normalized_text: STREAM frames received after sending STOP_SENDING are still counted toward the connection and stream flow-control windows, even though these frames will be discarded upon receipt.
clauses.raw_text: STREAM frames received after sending STOP_SENDING are still counted toward the connection and stream flow-control windows, even though these frames will be discarded upon receipt.

clauses.normalized_text: This avoids potential ambiguity about which STREAM frames count toward flow control.
clauses.raw_text: This avoids potential ambiguity about which STREAM frames count toward flow control.

clauses.normalized_text: A STOP_SENDING frame requests that the receiving endpoint send a RST_STREAM frame.
clauses.raw_text: A STOP_SENDING frame requests that the receiving endpoint send a RST_STREAM frame.

clauses.normalized_text: An endpoint that receives a STOP_SENDING frame MUST send a RST_STREAM frame for that stream, and can use an error code of STOPPING.
clauses.raw_text: An endpoint that receives a STOP_SENDING frame MUST send a RST_STREAM frame for that stream, and can use an error code of STOPPING.

clauses.normalized_text: If the STOP_SENDING frame is received on a send stream that is already in the “Data Sent” state, a RST_STREAM frame MAY still be sent in order to cancel retransmission of previously-sent STREAM frames.
clauses.raw_text: If the STOP_SENDING frame is received on a send stream that is already in the “Data Sent” state, a RST_STREAM frame MAY still be sent in order to cancel retransmission of previously-sent STREAM frames.

clauses.normalized_text: STOP_SENDING SHOULD only be sent for a receive stream that has not been reset.
clauses.raw_text: STOP_SENDING SHOULD only be sent for a receive stream that has not been reset.

clauses.normalized_text: STOP_SENDING is most useful for streams in the “Recv” or “Size Known” states.
clauses.raw_text: STOP_SENDING is most useful for streams in the “Recv” or “Size Known” states.

clauses.normalized_text: An endpoint is expected to send another STOP_SENDING frame if a packet containing a previous STOP_SENDING is lost.
clauses.raw_text: An endpoint is expected to send another STOP_SENDING frame if a packet containing a previous STOP_SENDING is lost.

clauses.normalized_text: All QUIC frames are idempotent.
clauses.raw_text: All QUIC frames are idempotent.

clauses.normalized_text: That is, a valid frame does not cause undesirable side effects or errors when received more than once.
clauses.raw_text: That is, a valid frame does not cause undesirable side effects or errors when received more than once.

clauses.normalized_text: The Frame Type field uses a variable length integer encoding (see [integer-encoding]) with one exception.
clauses.raw_text: The Frame Type field uses a variable length integer encoding (see [integer-encoding]) with one exception.

clauses.normalized_text: To ensure simple and efficient implementations of frame parsing, a frame type MUST use the shortest possible encoding.
clauses.raw_text: To ensure simple and efficient implementations of frame parsing, a frame type MUST use the shortest possible encoding.

clauses.normalized_text: Though a two-, four- or eight-octet encoding of the frame types defined in this document is possible, the Frame Type field for these frames is encoded on a single octet.
clauses.raw_text: Though a two-, four- or eight-octet encoding of the frame types defined in this document is possible, the Frame Type field for these frames is encoded on a single octet.

clauses.raw_text: For instance, though 0x4007 is a legitimate two-octet encoding for a variable-length integer with a value of 7, PING frames are always encoded as a single octet with the value 0x07.

clauses.normalized_text: An endpoint MUST treat the receipt of a frame type that uses a longer encoding than necessary as a connection error of type PROTOCOL_VIOLATION.

clauses.normalized_text: A sender bundles one or more frames in a QUIC packet (see [frames]).
clauses.raw_text: A sender bundles one or more frames in a QUIC packet (see [frames]).

clauses.normalized_text: A sender can minimize per-packet bandwidth and computational costs by bundling as many frames as possible within a QUIC packet.
clauses.raw_text: A sender can minimize per-packet bandwidth and computational costs by bundling as many frames as possible within a QUIC packet.

clauses.normalized_text: A sender MAY wait for a short period of time to bundle multiple frames before sending a packet that is not maximally packed, to avoid sending out large numbers of small packets.
clauses.raw_text: A sender MAY wait for a short period of time to bundle multiple frames before sending a packet that is not maximally packed, to avoid sending out large numbers of small packets.

clauses.normalized_text: An implementation may use knowledge about application sending behavior or heuristics to determine whether and for how long to wait.
clauses.raw_text: An implementation may use knowledge about application sending behavior or heuristics to determine whether and for how long to wait.

clauses.normalized_text: This waiting period is an implementation decision, and an implementation should be careful to delay conservatively, since any delay is likely to increase application-visible latency.
clauses.raw_text: This waiting period is an implementation decision, and an implementation should be careful to delay conservatively, since any delay is likely to increase application-visible latency.

clauses.normalized_text: Stream multiplexing is achieved by interleaving STREAM frames from multiple streams into one or more QUIC packets.
clauses.raw_text: Stream multiplexing is achieved by interleaving STREAM frames from multiple streams into one or more QUIC packets.

clauses.normalized_text: A single QUIC packet can include multiple STREAM frames from one or more streams.
clauses.raw_text: A single QUIC packet can include multiple STREAM frames from one or more streams.

clauses.normalized_text: One of the benefits of QUIC is avoidance of head-of-line blocking across multiple streams.
clauses.raw_text: One of the benefits of QUIC is avoidance of head-of-line blocking across multiple streams.

clauses.normalized_text: When a packet loss occurs, only streams with data in that packet are blocked waiting for a retransmission to be received, while other streams can continue making progress.
clauses.raw_text: When a packet loss occurs, only streams with data in that packet are blocked waiting for a retransmission to be received, while other streams can continue making progress.

clauses.normalized_text: Note that when data from multiple streams is bundled into a single QUIC packet, loss of that packet blocks all those streams from making progress.
clauses.raw_text: Note that when data from multiple streams is bundled into a single QUIC packet, loss of that packet blocks all those streams from making progress.

clauses.normalized_text: Implementations are advised to bundle as few streams as necessary in outgoing packets without losing transmission efficiency to underfilled packets.
clauses.raw_text: Implementations are advised to bundle as few streams as necessary in outgoing packets without losing transmission efficiency to underfilled packets.

clauses.normalized_text: A packet MUST NOT be acknowledged until packet protection has been successfully removed and all frames contained in the packet have been processed.
clauses.raw_text: A packet MUST NOT be acknowledged until packet protection has been successfully removed and all frames contained in the packet have been processed.

clauses.normalized_text: For STREAM frames, this means the data has been enqueued in preparation to be received by the application protocol, but it does not require that data is delivered and consumed.
clauses.raw_text: For STREAM frames, this means the data has been enqueued in preparation to be received by the application protocol, but it does not require that data is delivered and consumed.

clauses.normalized_text: Once the packet has been fully processed, a receiver acknowledges receipt by sending one or more ACK frames containing the packet number of the received packet.
clauses.raw_text: Once the packet has been fully processed, a receiver acknowledges receipt by sending one or more ACK frames containing the packet number of the received packet.

clauses.normalized_text: To avoid creating an indefinite feedback loop, an endpoint MUST NOT send an ACK frame in response to a packet containing only ACK or PADDING frames, even if there are packet gaps which precede the received packet.
clauses.raw_text: To avoid creating an indefinite feedback loop, an endpoint MUST NOT send an ACK frame in response to a packet containing only ACK or PADDING frames, even if there are packet gaps which precede the received packet.

clauses.normalized_text: The endpoint MUST however acknowledge packets containing only ACK or PADDING frames when sending ACK frames in response to other packets.
clauses.raw_text: The endpoint MUST however acknowledge packets containing only ACK or PADDING frames when sending ACK frames in response to other packets.

clauses.normalized_text: While PADDING frames do not elicit an ACK frame from a receiver, they are considered to be in flight for congestion control purposes [QUIC-RECOVERY].
clauses.raw_text: While PADDING frames do not elicit an ACK frame from a receiver, they are considered to be in flight for congestion control purposes [QUIC-RECOVERY].

clauses.normalized_text: Sending only PADDING frames might cause the sender to become limited by the congestion controller (as described in [QUIC-RECOVERY]) with no acknowledgments forthcoming from the receiver.
clauses.raw_text: Sending only PADDING frames might cause the sender to become limited by the congestion controller (as described in [QUIC-RECOVERY]) with no acknowledgments forthcoming from the receiver.

clauses.normalized_text: Therefore, a sender should ensure that other frames are sent in addition to PADDING frames to elicit acknowledgments from the receiver.
clauses.raw_text: Therefore, a sender should ensure that other frames are sent in addition to PADDING frames to elicit acknowledgments from the receiver.

clauses.normalized_text: An endpoint MUST NOT send more than one packet containing only an ACK frame per received packet that contains frames other than ACK and PADDING frames.
clauses.raw_text: An endpoint MUST NOT send more than one packet containing only an ACK frame per received packet that contains frames other than ACK and PADDING frames.

clauses.normalized_text: The receiver’s delayed acknowledgment timer SHOULD NOT exceed the current RTT estimate or the value it indicates in the max_ack_delay transport parameter.
clauses.raw_text: The receiver’s delayed acknowledgment timer SHOULD NOT exceed the current RTT estimate or the value it indicates in the max_ack_delay transport parameter.

clauses.normalized_text: This ensures an acknowledgment is sent at least once per RTT when packets needing acknowledgement are received.
clauses.raw_text: This ensures an acknowledgment is sent at least once per RTT when packets needing acknowledgement are received.

clauses.normalized_text: The sender can use the receiver’s max_ack_delay value in determining timeouts for timer-based retransmission.
clauses.raw_text: The sender can use the receiver’s max_ack_delay value in determining timeouts for timer-based retransmission.

clauses.normalized_text: Strategies and implications of the frequency of generating acknowledgments are discussed in more detail in [QUIC-RECOVERY].
clauses.raw_text: Strategies and implications of the frequency of generating acknowledgments are discussed in more detail in [QUIC-RECOVERY].

clauses.normalized_text: To limit ACK Blocks to those that have not yet been received by the sender, the receiver SHOULD track which ACK frames have been acknowledged by its peer.
clauses.raw_text: To limit ACK Blocks to those that have not yet been received by the sender, the receiver SHOULD track which ACK frames have been acknowledged by its peer.

clauses.normalized_text: Once an ACK frame has been acknowledged, the packets it acknowledges SHOULD NOT be acknowledged again.
clauses.raw_text: Once an ACK frame has been acknowledged, the packets it acknowledges SHOULD NOT be acknowledged again.

clauses.normalized_text: Because ACK frames are not sent in response to ACK-only packets, a receiver that is only sending ACK frames will only receive acknowledgements for its packets if the sender includes them in packets with non-ACK frames.
clauses.raw_text: Because ACK frames are not sent in response to ACK-only packets, a receiver that is only sending ACK frames will only receive acknowledgements for its packets if the sender includes them in packets with non-ACK frames.

clauses.normalized_text: A sender SHOULD bundle ACK frames with other frames when possible.
clauses.raw_text: A sender SHOULD bundle ACK frames with other frames when possible.

clauses.raw_text: To limit receiver state or the size of ACK frames, a receiver MAY limit the number of ACK Blocks it sends.

clauses.normalized_text: A receiver can do this even without receiving acknowledgment of its ACK frames, with the knowledge this could cause the sender to unnecessarily retransmit some data.
clauses.raw_text: A receiver can do this even without receiving acknowledgment of its ACK frames, with the knowledge this could cause the sender to unnecessarily retransmit some data.

clauses.normalized_text: Standard QUIC [QUIC-RECOVERY] algorithms declare packets lost after sufficiently newer packets are acknowledged.
clauses.raw_text: Standard QUIC [QUIC-RECOVERY] algorithms declare packets lost after sufficiently newer packets are acknowledged.

clauses.normalized_text: Therefore, the receiver SHOULD repeatedly acknowledge newly received packets in preference to packets received in the past.
clauses.raw_text: Therefore, the receiver SHOULD repeatedly acknowledge newly received packets in preference to packets received in the past.

clauses.normalized_text: ACK frames MUST only be carried in a packet that has the same packet number space as the packet being ACKed (see [packet-protected]).
clauses.raw_text: ACK frames MUST only be carried in a packet that has the same packet number space as the packet being ACKed (see [packet-protected]).

clauses.normalized_text: For instance, packets that are protected with 1-RTT keys MUST be acknowledged in packets that are also protected with 1-RTT keys.
clauses.raw_text: For instance, packets that are protected with 1-RTT keys MUST be acknowledged in packets that are also protected with 1-RTT keys.

clauses.normalized_text: Packets that a client sends with 0-RTT packet protection MUST be acknowledged by the server in packets protected by 1-RTT keys.
clauses.raw_text: Packets that a client sends with 0-RTT packet protection MUST be acknowledged by the server in packets protected by 1-RTT keys.

clauses.raw_text: This can mean that the client is unable to use these acknowledgments if the server cryptographic handshake messages are delayed or lost.

clauses.raw_text: Note that the same limitation applies to other data sent by the server protected by the 1-RTT keys.

clauses.raw_text: Endpoints SHOULD send acknowledgments for packets containing CRYPTO frames with a reduced delay; see Section 4.3.1 of [QUIC-RECOVERY].

clauses.raw_text: The same applies to the frames that are contained within lost packets.

clauses.raw_text: Instead, the information that might be carried in frames is sent again in new frames as needed.

clauses.raw_text: New frames and packets are used to carry information that is determined to have been lost.

clauses.raw_text: Data sent in CRYPTO frames is retransmitted according to the rules in [QUIC-RECOVERY], until all data has been acknowledged.

clauses.raw_text: Once an endpoint sends a RST_STREAM frame, no further STREAM frames are needed.

clauses.normalized_text: The most recent set of acknowledgments are sent in ACK frames.
clauses.raw_text: The most recent set of acknowledgments are sent in ACK frames.

clauses.normalized_text: An ACK frame SHOULD contain all unacknowledged acknowledgments, as described in [sending-ack-frames].
clauses.raw_text: An ACK frame SHOULD contain all unacknowledged acknowledgments, as described in [sending-ack-frames].

clauses.normalized_text: QUIC endpoints use Explicit Congestion Notification (ECN) [RFC3168] to detect and respond to network congestion.
clauses.raw_text: QUIC endpoints use Explicit Congestion Notification (ECN) [RFC3168] to detect and respond to network congestion.

clauses.raw_text: ECN allows a network node to indicate congestion in the network by setting a codepoint in the IP header of a packet instead of dropping it.

clauses.raw_text: Endpoints react to congestion by reducing their sending rate in response, as described in [QUIC-RECOVERY].

clauses.normalized_text: To use ECN, QUIC endpoints first determine whether a path supports ECN marking and the peer is able to access the ECN codepoint in the IP header.
clauses.raw_text: To use ECN, QUIC endpoints first determine whether a path supports ECN marking and the peer is able to access the ECN codepoint in the IP header.

clauses.normalized_text: A network path does not support ECN if ECN marked packets get dropped or ECN markings are rewritten on the path.
clauses.raw_text: A network path does not support ECN if ECN marked packets get dropped or ECN markings are rewritten on the path.

clauses.normalized_text: An endpoint verifies the path, both during connection establishment and when migrating to a new path (see [migration]).
clauses.raw_text: An endpoint verifies the path, both during connection establishment and when migrating to a new path (see [migration]).

clauses.normalized_text: On receiving a packet with an ECT or CE codepoint, an endpoint that can access the IP ECN codepoints increases the corresponding ECT(0), ECT(1), or CE count, and includes these counters in subsequent (see [processing-and-ack]) ACK frames (see [frame-ack]).
clauses.raw_text: On receiving a packet with an ECT or CE codepoint, an endpoint that can access the IP ECN codepoints increases the corresponding ECT(0), ECT(1), or CE count, and includes these counters in subsequent (see [processing-and-ack]) ACK frames (see [frame-ack]).

clauses.normalized_text: A packet detected by a receiver as a duplicate does not affect the receiver’s local ECN codepoint counts; see ([security-ecn]) for relevant security concerns.
clauses.raw_text: A packet detected by a receiver as a duplicate does not affect the receiver’s local ECN codepoint counts; see ([security-ecn]) for relevant security concerns.

clauses.normalized_text: If an endpoint receives a packet without an ECT or CE codepoint, it responds per [processing-and-ack] with an ACK frame.
clauses.raw_text: If an endpoint receives a packet without an ECT or CE codepoint, it responds per [processing-and-ack] with an ACK frame.

clauses.normalized_text: If an endpoint does not have access to received ECN codepoints, it acknowledges received packets per [processing-and-ack] with an ACK frame.
clauses.raw_text: If an endpoint does not have access to received ECN codepoints, it acknowledges received packets per [processing-and-ack] with an ACK frame.

clauses.normalized_text: Each endpoint independently verifies and enables use of ECN by setting the IP header ECN codepoint to ECN Capable Transport (ECT) for the path from it to the other peer.
clauses.raw_text: Each endpoint independently verifies and enables use of ECN by setting the IP header ECN codepoint to ECN Capable Transport (ECT) for the path from it to the other peer.

clauses.normalized_text: Even if ECN is not used on the path to the peer, the endpoint MUST provide feedback about ECN markings received (if accessible).
clauses.raw_text: Even if ECN is not used on the path to the peer, the endpoint MUST provide feedback about ECN markings received (if accessible).

clauses.normalized_text: To verify both that a path supports ECN and the peer can provide ECN feedback, an endpoint MUST set the ECT(0) codepoint in the IP header of all outgoing packets [RFC8311].
clauses.raw_text: To verify both that a path supports ECN and the peer can provide ECN feedback, an endpoint MUST set the ECT(0) codepoint in the IP header of all outgoing packets [RFC8311].

clauses.normalized_text: If an ECT codepoint set in the IP header is not corrupted by a network device, then a received packet contains either the codepoint sent by the peer or the Congestion Experienced (CE) codepoint set by a network device that is experiencing congestion.
clauses.raw_text: If an ECT codepoint set in the IP header is not corrupted by a network device, then a received packet contains either the codepoint sent by the peer or the Congestion Experienced (CE) codepoint set by a network device that is experiencing congestion.

clauses.normalized_text: If a packet sent with an ECT codepoint is newly acknowledged by the peer in an ACK frame without ECN feedback, the endpoint stops setting ECT codepoints in subsequent packets, with the expectation that either the network or the peer no longer supports ECN.

clauses.normalized_text: To protect the connection from arbitrary corruption of ECN codepoints by the network, an endpoint verifies the following when an ACK frame is received:
clauses.raw_text: To protect the connection from arbitrary corruption of ECN codepoints by the network, an endpoint verifies the following when an ACK frame is received:

clauses.normalized_text: The increase in ECT(0) and ECT(1) counters MUST be at least the number of packets newly acknowledged that were sent with the corresponding codepoint.
clauses.raw_text: The increase in ECT(0) and ECT(1) counters MUST be at least the number of packets newly acknowledged that were sent with the corresponding codepoint.

clauses.normalized_text: The total increase in ECT(0), ECT(1), and CE counters reported in the ACK frame MUST be at least the total number of packets newly acknowledged in this ACK frame.
clauses.raw_text: The total increase in ECT(0), ECT(1), and CE counters reported in the ACK frame MUST be at least the total number of packets newly acknowledged in this ACK frame.

clauses.normalized_text: An endpoint could miss acknowledgements for a packet when ACK frames are lost.
clauses.raw_text: An endpoint could miss acknowledgements for a packet when ACK frames are lost.

clauses.normalized_text: It is therefore possible for the total increase in ECT(0), ECT(1), and CE counters to be greater than the number of packets acknowledged in an ACK frame.
clauses.raw_text: It is therefore possible for the total increase in ECT(0), ECT(1), and CE counters to be greater than the number of packets acknowledged in an ACK frame.

clauses.normalized_text: When this happens, the local reference counts MUST be increased to match the counters in the ACK frame.
clauses.raw_text: When this happens, the local reference counts MUST be increased to match the counters in the ACK frame.

clauses.normalized_text: Upon successful verification, an endpoint continues to set ECT codepoints in subsequent packets with the expectation that the path is ECN-capable.
clauses.raw_text: Upon successful verification, an endpoint continues to set ECT codepoints in subsequent packets with the expectation that the path is ECN-capable.

clauses.normalized_text: If verification fails, then the endpoint ceases setting ECT codepoints in subsequent packets with the expectation that either the network or the peer does not support ECN.
clauses.raw_text: If verification fails, then the endpoint ceases setting ECT codepoints in subsequent packets with the expectation that either the network or the peer does not support ECN.

clauses.normalized_text: If an endpoint sets ECT codepoints on outgoing packets and encounters a retransmission timeout due to the absence of acknowledgments from the peer (see [QUIC-RECOVERY]), or if an endpoint has reason to believe that a network element might be corrupting ECN codepoints, the endpoint MAY cease setting ECT codepoints in subsequent packets.
clauses.raw_text: If an endpoint sets ECT codepoints on outgoing packets and encounters a retransmission timeout due to the absence of acknowledgments from the peer (see [QUIC-RECOVERY]), or if an endpoint has reason to believe that a network element might be corrupting ECN codepoints, the endpoint MAY cease setting ECT codepoints in subsequent packets.

clauses.normalized_text: Doing so allows the connection to traverse network elements that drop or corrupt ECN codepoints in the IP header.
clauses.raw_text: Doing so allows the connection to traverse network elements that drop or corrupt ECN codepoints in the IP header.

clauses.normalized_text: The QUIC packet size includes the QUIC header and integrity check, but not the UDP or IP header.
clauses.raw_text: The QUIC packet size includes the QUIC header and integrity check, but not the UDP or IP header.

clauses.normalized_text: Clients MUST ensure that the first Initial packet they send is sent in a UDP datagram that is at least 1200 octets.
clauses.raw_text: Clients MUST ensure that the first Initial packet they send is sent in a UDP datagram that is at least 1200 octets.

clauses.normalized_text: Padding the Initial packet or including a 0-RTT packet in the same datagram are ways to meet this requirement.
clauses.raw_text: Padding the Initial packet or including a 0-RTT packet in the same datagram are ways to meet this requirement.

clauses.normalized_text: Sending a UDP datagram of this size ensures that the network path supports a reasonable Maximum Transmission Unit (MTU), and helps reduce the amplitude of amplification attacks caused by server responses toward an unverified client address, see [address-validation].
clauses.raw_text: Sending a UDP datagram of this size ensures that the network path supports a reasonable Maximum Transmission Unit (MTU), and helps reduce the amplitude of amplification attacks caused by server responses toward an unverified client address, see [address-validation].

clauses.normalized_text: The payload of a UDP datagram carrying the Initial packet MUST be expanded to at least 1200 octets, by adding PADDING frames to the Initial packet and/or by combining the Initial packet with a 0-RTT packet (see [packet-coalesce]).
clauses.raw_text: The payload of a UDP datagram carrying the Initial packet MUST be expanded to at least 1200 octets, by adding PADDING frames to the Initial packet and/or by combining the Initial packet with a 0-RTT packet (see [packet-coalesce]).

clauses.normalized_text: The datagram containing the first Initial packet from a client MAY exceed 1200 octets if the client believes that the Path Maximum Transmission Unit (PMTU) supports the size that it chooses.
clauses.raw_text: The datagram containing the first Initial packet from a client MAY exceed 1200 octets if the client believes that the Path Maximum Transmission Unit (PMTU) supports the size that it chooses.

clauses.normalized_text: A server MAY send a CONNECTION_CLOSE frame with error code PROTOCOL_VIOLATION in response to the first Initial packet it receives from a client if the UDP datagram is smaller than 1200 octets.
clauses.raw_text: A server MAY send a CONNECTION_CLOSE frame with error code PROTOCOL_VIOLATION in response to the first Initial packet it receives from a client if the UDP datagram is smaller than 1200 octets.

clauses.normalized_text: It MUST NOT send any other frame type in response, or otherwise behave as if any part of the offending packet was processed as valid.
clauses.raw_text: It MUST NOT send any other frame type in response, or otherwise behave as if any part of the offending packet was processed as valid.

clauses.normalized_text: The server MUST also limit the number of bytes it sends before validating the address of the client, see [address-validation].
clauses.raw_text: The server MUST also limit the number of bytes it sends before validating the address of the client, see [address-validation].

clauses.normalized_text: The Path Maximum Transmission Unit (PMTU) is the maximum size of the entire IP header, UDP header, and UDP payload.
clauses.raw_text: The Path Maximum Transmission Unit (PMTU) is the maximum size of the entire IP header, UDP header, and UDP payload.

clauses.normalized_text: The UDP payload includes the QUIC packet header, protected payload, and any authentication fields.
clauses.raw_text: The UDP payload includes the QUIC packet header, protected payload, and any authentication fields.

clauses.normalized_text: All QUIC packets SHOULD be sized to fit within the estimated PMTU to avoid IP fragmentation or packet drops.
clauses.raw_text: All QUIC packets SHOULD be sized to fit within the estimated PMTU to avoid IP fragmentation or packet drops.

clauses.normalized_text: To optimize bandwidth efficiency, endpoints SHOULD use Packetization Layer PMTU Discovery ([PLPMTUD]).
clauses.raw_text: To optimize bandwidth efficiency, endpoints SHOULD use Packetization Layer PMTU Discovery ([PLPMTUD]).

clauses.normalized_text: Endpoints MAY use PMTU Discovery ([PMTUDv4], [PMTUDv6]) for detecting the PMTU, setting the PMTU appropriately, and storing the result of previous PMTU determinations.
clauses.raw_text: Endpoints MAY use PMTU Discovery ([PMTUDv4], [PMTUDv6]) for detecting the PMTU, setting the PMTU appropriately, and storing the result of previous PMTU determinations.

clauses.normalized_text: In the absence of these mechanisms, QUIC endpoints SHOULD NOT send IP packets larger than 1280 octets.
clauses.raw_text: In the absence of these mechanisms, QUIC endpoints SHOULD NOT send IP packets larger than 1280 octets.

clauses.raw_text: Assuming the minimum IP header size, this results in a QUIC packet size of 1232 octets for IPv6 and 1252 octets for IPv4.

clauses.raw_text: Some QUIC implementations MAY be more conservative in computing allowed QUIC packet size given unknown tunneling overheads or IP header options.

clauses.normalized_text: QUIC endpoints that implement any kind of PMTU discovery SHOULD maintain an estimate for each combination of local and remote IP addresses.
clauses.raw_text: QUIC endpoints that implement any kind of PMTU discovery SHOULD maintain an estimate for each combination of local and remote IP addresses.

clauses.normalized_text: Each pairing of local and remote addresses could have a different maximum MTU in the path.
clauses.raw_text: Each pairing of local and remote addresses could have a different maximum MTU in the path.

clauses.normalized_text: QUIC depends on the network path supporting an MTU of at least 1280 octets.
clauses.raw_text: QUIC depends on the network path supporting an MTU of at least 1280 octets.

clauses.normalized_text: This is the IPv6 minimum MTU and therefore also supported by most modern IPv4 networks.
clauses.raw_text: This is the IPv6 minimum MTU and therefore also supported by most modern IPv4 networks.

clauses.normalized_text: An endpoint MUST NOT reduce its MTU below this number, even if it receives signals that indicate a smaller limit might exist.
clauses.raw_text: An endpoint MUST NOT reduce its MTU below this number, even if it receives signals that indicate a smaller limit might exist.

clauses.normalized_text: If a QUIC endpoint determines that the PMTU between any pair of local and remote IP addresses has fallen below 1280 octets, it MUST immediately cease sending QUIC packets on the affected path.
clauses.raw_text: If a QUIC endpoint determines that the PMTU between any pair of local and remote IP addresses has fallen below 1280 octets, it MUST immediately cease sending QUIC packets on the affected path.

clauses.normalized_text: This could result in termination of the connection if an alternative path cannot be found.
clauses.raw_text: This could result in termination of the connection if an alternative path cannot be found.

clauses.normalized_text: Traditional ICMP-based path MTU discovery in IPv4 [PMTUDv4] is potentially vulnerable to off-path attacks that successfully guess the IP/port 4-tuple and reduce the MTU to a bandwidth-inefficient value.
clauses.raw_text: Traditional ICMP-based path MTU discovery in IPv4 [PMTUDv4] is potentially vulnerable to off-path attacks that successfully guess the IP/port 4-tuple and reduce the MTU to a bandwidth-inefficient value.

clauses.normalized_text: TCP connections mitigate this risk by using the (at minimum) 8 bytes of transport header echoed in the ICMP message to validate the TCP sequence number as valid for the current connection.
clauses.raw_text: TCP connections mitigate this risk by using the (at minimum) 8 bytes of transport header echoed in the ICMP message to validate the TCP sequence number as valid for the current connection.

clauses.normalized_text: However, as QUIC operates over UDP, in IPv4 the echoed information could consist only of the IP and UDP headers, which usually has insufficient entropy to mitigate off-path attacks.
clauses.raw_text: However, as QUIC operates over UDP, in IPv4 the echoed information could consist only of the IP and UDP headers, which usually has insufficient entropy to mitigate off-path attacks.

clauses.normalized_text: As a result, endpoints that implement PMTUD in IPv4 SHOULD take steps to mitigate this risk.
clauses.raw_text: As a result, endpoints that implement PMTUD in IPv4 SHOULD take steps to mitigate this risk.

clauses.normalized_text: For instance, an application could:
clauses.raw_text: For instance, an application could:

clauses.normalized_text: Set the IPv4 Don’t Fragment (DF) bit on a small proportion of packets, so that most invalid ICMP messages arrive when there are no DF packets outstanding, and can therefore be identified as spurious.
clauses.raw_text: Set the IPv4 Don’t Fragment (DF) bit on a small proportion of packets, so that most invalid ICMP messages arrive when there are no DF packets outstanding, and can therefore be identified as spurious.

clauses.normalized_text: Store additional information from the IP or UDP headers from DF packets (for example, the IP ID or UDP checksum) to further authenticate incoming Datagram Too Big messages.
clauses.raw_text: Store additional information from the IP or UDP headers from DF packets (for example, the IP ID or UDP checksum) to further authenticate incoming Datagram Too Big messages.

clauses.normalized_text: QUIC packets and frames commonly use a variable-length encoding for non-negative integer values.
clauses.raw_text: QUIC packets and frames commonly use a variable-length encoding for non-negative integer values.

clauses.normalized_text: This encoding ensures that smaller integer values need fewer octets to encode.
clauses.raw_text: This encoding ensures that smaller integer values need fewer octets to encode.

clauses.normalized_text: The QUIC variable-length integer encoding reserves the two most significant bits of the first octet to encode the base 2 logarithm of the integer encoding length in octets.
clauses.raw_text: The QUIC variable-length integer encoding reserves the two most significant bits of the first octet to encode the base 2 logarithm of the integer encoding length in octets.

clauses.normalized_text: The integer value is encoded on the remaining bits, in network byte order.
clauses.raw_text: The integer value is encoded on the remaining bits, in network byte order.

clauses.normalized_text: This means that integers are encoded on 1, 2, 4, or 8 octets and can encode 6, 14, 30, or 62 bit values respectively. [integer-summary] summarizes the encoding properties.
clauses.raw_text: This means that integers are encoded on 1, 2, 4, or 8 octets and can encode 6, 14, 30, or 62 bit values respectively. [integer-summary] summarizes the encoding properties.

clauses.normalized_text: For example, the eight octet sequence c2 19 7c 5e ff 14 e8 8c (in hexadecimal) decodes to the decimal value 151288809941952652; the four octet sequence 9d 7f 3e 7d decodes to 494878333; the two octet sequence 7b bd decodes to 15293; and the single octet 25 decodes to 37 (as does the two octet sequence 40 25).
clauses.raw_text: For example, the eight octet sequence c2 19 7c 5e ff 14 e8 8c (in hexadecimal) decodes to the decimal value 151288809941952652; the four octet sequence 9d 7f 3e 7d decodes to 494878333; the two octet sequence 7b bd decodes to 15293; and the single octet 25 decodes to 37 (as does the two octet sequence 40 25).

clauses.normalized_text: A peer receiving the packet will then correctly decode the packet number, unless the packet is delayed in transit such that it arrives after many higher-numbered packets have been received.

clauses.normalized_text: An endpoint SHOULD use a large enough packet number encoding to allow the packet number to be recovered even if the packet arrives after packets that are sent afterwards.
clauses.raw_text: An endpoint SHOULD use a large enough packet number encoding to allow the packet number to be recovered even if the packet arrives after packets that are sent afterwards.

clauses.normalized_text: As a result, the size of the packet number encoding is at least one more than the base 2 logarithm of the number of contiguous unacknowledged packet numbers, including the new packet.

clauses.normalized_text: For example, if an endpoint has received an acknowledgment for packet 0x6afa2f, sending a packet with a number of 0x6b2d79 requires a packet number encoding with 14 bits or more; whereas the 30-bit packet number encoding is needed to send a packet with a number of 0x6bc107.

clauses.normalized_text: At a receiver, protection of the packet number is removed prior to recovering the full packet number.
clauses.raw_text: At a receiver, protection of the packet number is removed prior to recovering the full packet number.

clauses.normalized_text: The full packet number is then reconstructed based on the number of significant bits present, the value of those bits, and the largest packet number received on a successfully authenticated packet.
clauses.raw_text: The full packet number is then reconstructed based on the number of significant bits present, the value of those bits, and the largest packet number received on a successfully authenticated packet.

clauses.normalized_text: Recovering the full packet number is necessary to successfully remove packet protection.
clauses.raw_text: Recovering the full packet number is necessary to successfully remove packet protection.

clauses.normalized_text: Once packet number protection is removed, the packet number is decoded by finding the packet number value that is closest to the next expected packet.
clauses.raw_text: Once packet number protection is removed, the packet number is decoded by finding the packet number value that is closest to the next expected packet.

clauses.normalized_text: The next expected packet is the highest received packet number plus one.
clauses.raw_text: The next expected packet is the highest received packet number plus one.

clauses.normalized_text: For example, if the highest successfully authenticated packet had a packet number of 0xaa82f30e, then a packet containing a 14-bit value of 0x9b3 will be decoded as 0xaa8309b3.
clauses.raw_text: For example, if the highest successfully authenticated packet had a packet number of 0xaa82f30e, then a packet containing a 14-bit value of 0x9b3 will be decoded as 0xaa8309b3.

clauses.raw_text: Example pseudo-code for packet number decoding can be found in [sample-packet-number-decoding].
